questions.question: Who among the following introduced the ’Doctrine of Lapse’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The doctrine of lapse, **a formula formulated by Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India (1848–56), to deal with questions of succession in Hindu Indian states.**
 
• According to this policy,** if the king did not have any natural-born heir then the kingdom would lapse to the British or would be administered and occupied by the British.**
 
• Indian states such as **Satara, Nagpur and Jhansi were annexed under this policy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Dalhousie**

 
 
• **​**On 12 January 1848,** he was appointed Governor-General of India and Governor of Bengal**.
 
• Dalhousie considered **the consolidation of British power in India **as its main objective.
 
• He was responsible for introducing many modern reforms in India **such as railways, telegraph and postal networks and public works.​**
 
• ​​He is best remembered for** the Doctrine of Lapse Policy, which many attributes directly to the Indian Rebellion of 1857.**
 
• Lord Dalhousie also started many **Anglo-vernacular schools in India**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Ripon**
 
 
• **​**Viceroy of India from 1880-84.
 
• **The Vernacular Press Act was cancelled in 1882**.
 
• The first Factory Act was implemented in 1881.
 
 
 
• **Warren Hastings**
 
 
• ​First Governor of the Presidency of Fort Williams.
 
• **First Governor-General of Bengal.**
 
• Warren Hastings played an important role in the **abolition of dual system.**
 
• To collect the **revenue a Board of Revenue was set up at Calcutta**.

questions.question: Ryotwari system of revenue collection in India, introduced by the British, was based on the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ricardian theory of rent.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ryotwari system:-**

 
 
• The Ryotwari system​ **of revenue collection** in India was introduced by the **British **during their colonial rule.
 
• This system was based on the** Ricardian theory of rent, **which states that rent is the** surplus income** earned by landowners due to the** differential fertility of land.**
 
• Under the Ryotwari system, individual farmers or ryots were directly responsible for **paying land revenue **to the government.
 
• This system was prevalent in areas where** landownership was fragmented** and there were no intermediaries between the government and the farmers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smith's theory :-**

 
 
• It​** **is based on the idea that rent is **paid for the use of land **that has a** fixed supply and is immobile.**
 
 
 
• **Malthusian theory :-**
 
 
• It suggests that as **population growth increases**, land becomes scarce and rents increase, leading to a **decline in living standards. **
 
 
 
• **Marx's theory :-**
 
 
• It​** **is based on the idea that rent is a** form of exploitation of the labor of tenant farmers **by landowners who hold a monopoly on land.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Lord Curzon** was the **Viceroy of India **from** 1899 to 1905 **and he announced the** partition of Bengal in 1905.**
 
• The partition of Bengal was a British colonial policy that aimed to weaken the** nationalist movement in India **by dividing Bengal into two provinces, one **Hindu-majority **and the other **Muslim-majority.**
 
• The partition was widely opposed by **Indian nationalists**, who saw it as a deliberate attempt to divide and rule the country.
 
• The partition was eventually revoked in **1911**, due to sustained protests and political pressure from **Indian nationalists.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In order to deny Indians the right to self-governance, the** Lord Curzon's Calcutta Corporation Act of 1899** increased the number of nominated officials while decreasing the number of elected legislatures.
 
• After** 28 Corporation** members quit in protest, the Corporation was reorganized as a government department, with the majority of its employees being English and Anglo-Indian.

questions.question: Who among the following started the Kuka Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satguru Ram Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After the fall of the kingdom of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, there were several attempts to raise the old glory of the Khalsa.
 
• Several movements to reform the Sikhism were started.
 
• First, one being the Namdhari movement, which was started by Baba Ram Singh Namdhari after Anglo Sikh wars.
 
• He was a soldier in the Khalsa army.
 
• Like the Nirankari, this second reform movement known as the Namdhari, or Kuka, movement also had its origin in the north-west corner of the Sikh kingdom, away from the places of royal pomp and grandeur.
 
• It harked back to a way of life more in keeping with the spiritual tradition of the community.
 
• Its principal object was to spread the true spirit of Sikhism shorn of tawdry customs and mannerism, which had been growing on it since the beginning of the Sikh monarchy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the midst of national pride born of military glory and political power, this movement extolled the religious obligation for pious and simple living.
 
• They were called "Kukas" because of their particular style to recite the Gurbani (Sayings of the Gurus).
 
• This style was in a high pitched voice, called Kook in Punjabi, and thus Namdhari Khalsa’s were named Kukas.
 
• In the post-1857 phase of the freedom struggle, the Namdhari movement occupies a very significant place in the annals of history.
 
• It was founded at a time when the socio-religious teachings of the great Gurus were slowly being shadowed by other considerations and the political life was at its lowest ebb.
 
• Namdhari movement was an offshoot of Sikhism.
 
• The Kuka Movement was launched on the Baisakhi day in April 1857 at Bhaini (sahib), in Ludhiana District of Punjab.
 
• The leader of the Namdhari movement Baba Ram Singh was inspired by Maharaj Singh’s struggle against aliens and worked for social reforms and gave a call for the political battle against the Britishers.

questions.question: Which of the following associations was formed in Maharashtra to get social justice for the weaker sections of society?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The association formed in Maharashtra to get social justice for the weaker sections of society is the Satya Shodhak Samaj.
 
• Satya Shodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotirao Phule in 1873 with the aim to uplift the lower castes and women.
 
• **The movement challenged the** Brahminical domination** of the Indian society and advocated for social equality, education, and women's rights.**
 
• **The movement was instrumental in the** formation of the Indian National Congress and the Dalit movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theosophical Society**

 
 
• Theosophical Society is a worldwide organization that aims to promote unity and understanding among different religions and cultures.
 
• **It was founded in the United States in 1875 by Helena Petrovna Blavatsky, Henry Steel Olcott, and William Quan Judge.**
 
• The society's main objective is to study and promote theosophy, which is a set of spiritual and philosophical teachings that are believed to be universal and timeless.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj**
 
 
• ** Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 with the aim to promote Vedic knowledge and remove superstitions from Hinduism.**
 
• The movement emphasizes the authority of the Vedas and rejects idol worship, caste system, and animal sacrifices.
 
• Arya Samaj played an important role in the Indian independence movement and was a major influence on the Hindu nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Dharma Paripalana Yogam**
 
 
• Dharma Paripalana Yogam is a religious organization based in Kerala that aims to promote the teachings of Sree Narayana Guru, a social reformer and spiritual leader.
 
• **The organization is known for its work in the fields of education, healthcare, and social welfare.**
 
• Sree Narayana Guru is considered to be one of the most influential figures in the social reform movements of Kerala.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Diwani of Bengal transferred to the East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1765__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• **The Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the East India Company in 1765__.**
 
• **Diwani of Bengal- Result of Battle of Buxar**
 __
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought between the British and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, **Shuja Ud Daulah who was the Nawab of Awadh**, and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. This battle was won by the Britishers.
 
• The result of this battle was, the Diwani that is the right to collect the revenue of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha was sanctioned to the British by the Mughal Emperor in return for an annual sum of money and in the districts of Allahabad and Kora.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ 

 
• **Treaty of Allahabad**

 
 
• The Treaty of Allahabad was signed on **12 August 1765, between the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II,** son of the late Emperor Alamgir II, and Robert Clive, of the East India Company, in the aftermath of the Battle of Buxar of 23 October 1764.
